title: Sweden's PM was shot dead on a quiet street. 40 years later, the murder weapon still has no history.
description:
February 28, 1986. 11:21 PM. A single .357 Magnum round splits the Stockholm night on Sveavägen. Sweden's Prime Minister Olof Palme drops face-first onto the icy pavement. His wife Lisbet beside him, grazed in the back. They'd walked home from the Grand Cinema. No bodyguards. Palme had dismissed them — wanted to be a normal citizen. A second shot rings out.

Then footsteps, running south, gone. The revolver is found 30 hours later — a Smith & Wesson .357, serial number erased, abandoned on a sidewalk 400 meters away. It's never matched to a confirmed owner. Sweden launches the largest criminal investigation in its history. 90,000 people interviewed. 130 confessions received. None verified. The case goes cold for 34 years. Here's the twist.

In 2020, prosecutors name a suspect: Stig Engström, a graphic designer who worked near the murder scene. They close the case. But Engström killed himself in 2000. No trial. No confession. No physical evidence ties him to the gun. The murder weapon's serial number — ground down, never restored. The bullets pulled from Palme's body still sit in evidence, untraceable to any known firearm sale. One fact lingers: that night, someone in Stockholm had a revolver with no history. And 40 years later, it still has none.
